data.title: Rows and variables
data.prompt: A table has 5 units and 3 variables. One unit is removed and one variable is added. How many units and how many variables remain?
data.answer: Four units and four variables remain.

data.title: A mean is not the data
data.prompt: A paper reports only that the mean of ten heights is 170 cm. How many recorded heights are in that sentence?
data.answer: None. The sentence reports a summary. The ten heights are the data, and they are not shown.

dataset.title: Relative frequency after a deletion
dataset.prompt: The dataset of household sizes is 2, 4, 3, 2, 5. The household of size 5 is removed. What is the relative frequency of the value 2?
dataset.answer: The value 2 appears twice among the four remaining sizes, so the relative frequency is 2/4 = 1/2.

dataset.title: Mean of what remains
dataset.prompt: Using the same reduced dataset 2, 4, 3, 2, what is the mean?
dataset.answer: The total is 11 and there are 4 observations, so the mean is 11/4 = 2.75.

variable.title: Frequency of a category
variable.prompt: Six animals have species cat, dog, cat, cat, dog, rabbit. A seventh animal is a cat. How many cats are there?

variable.title: A code is not a mean of the category
variable.prompt: Pain is coded 1, 2, 3 for none, mild, and severe. The codes of three patients are 1, 3, and 2. Why is the average 2 not a pain?
variable.answer: The codes name ordered categories. Their average is an average of codes, not a pain on that scale.

levels-of-measurement.title: Mean of scores
levels-of-measurement.prompt: Five test scores are 90, 70, 80, 95, and 70. A sixth score of 85 is added. What is the mean of the six scores?
levels-of-measurement.answer: The total is 405 + 85 = 490. The mean is 490/6.

levels-of-measurement.title: Frequency of a grade
levels-of-measurement.prompt: Grades A, C, B, A, C are followed by one more grade B. How many times does B appear?

population.title: A new unit
population.prompt: Five workshops have outputs 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18. A sixth workshop with output 20 is added. What is the population mean?
population.answer: The total is 90 over 6 workshops, so the mean is 15.

population.title: A sample that does not change
population.prompt: In that same population, a sample of the two smallest outputs, 10 and 12, is kept after the sixth workshop is added. What is the sample mean?

sample.title: Enlarging a sample
sample.prompt: Population values are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The sample 2, 4, 6 is enlarged by the value 8. What is the new sample mean?
sample.answer: The sample values are 2, 4, 6, and 8. Their mean is 5.

sample.title: The population mean
sample.prompt: For the population 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, what is the population mean after that sample is enlarged?
sample.answer: The population is unchanged, so its mean remains 6.

census.title: Census mean of ten
census.prompt: Eight outputs sum to 50. Two more outputs, 7 and 9, are added and every workshop is observed. What is the census mean?
census.answer: The total is 66 over 10 workshops, so the mean is 6.6.

census.title: A sample that stays put
census.prompt: A sample of three outputs 5, 8, and 4 is not enlarged when those two workshops are added. What is the sample mean?

parameter.title: A new population mean
parameter.prompt: The values 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 are the whole population. A sixth value 16 is added to the population. What is the new population mean?
parameter.answer: The total is 46 over 6 values, so the mean is 46/6 = 23/3.

parameter.title: The statistic does not follow
parameter.prompt: The sample stays 2, 4, 6 after that sixth population value is added. What is the sample mean?

sampling-distribution.title: Expectation of the sample mean
sampling-distribution.prompt: From the population 1, 2, 3, the equally likely sample means of size 2 are 1.5, 2, and 2.5. What is their expectation?

sampling-distribution.title: Samples of size one
sampling-distribution.prompt: Samples of size 1 from 1, 2, 3 are equally likely. What is the expectation of that sampling distribution?

line-chart.title: A new household
line-chart.prompt: Sizes 2, 2, 3, 4, 2 gain one more household of size 3. What is the absolute frequency of 3?

line-chart.title: Relative frequency of 2
line-chart.prompt: After that addition there are six households and the value 2 still appears three times. What is the relative frequency of 2?

abundance-estimation.title: Petersen estimate
abundance-estimation.prompt: Twenty animals are marked, fifteen are caught later, and five of those are marked. What is the Petersen estimate?

abundance-estimation.title: Chapman estimate
abundance-estimation.prompt: For the same counts, what is the Chapman estimate (M+1)(C+1)/(R+1) − 1?

abundance-estimation.title: More recaptures
abundance-estimation.prompt: If 10 of the 15 animals in the second sample are marked, and 20 were marked at first, what is the Petersen estimate?

apriori-algorithm.title: Confidence
apriori-algorithm.prompt: In the four baskets {a,b}, {a,b}, {a} and {b,c}, what is the confidence of the rule a implies b?

apriori-algorithm.title: Lift
apriori-algorithm.prompt: What is the lift of that same rule?

apriori-algorithm.title: A rare pair
apriori-algorithm.prompt: What is the support of {b,c}, and does it pass a strict threshold of 2/5?
apriori-algorithm.answer: The support is 1/4, which does not pass a strict threshold of 2/5.

average-treatment-effect.title: Null average
average-treatment-effect.prompt: Eight patients have 4 deaths under treatment and 4 deaths under no treatment. What is the average treatment effect on the risk difference?
average-treatment-effect.answer: The risks are 4/8 and 4/8, so the average treatment effect is 0.

average-treatment-effect.title: One changed outcome
average-treatment-effect.prompt: After the last treated outcome changes from 1 to 0, 3 of 8 die under treatment and 4 of 8 die under no treatment. What is the average treatment effect?

base-rate.title: Mammogram predictive value
base-rate.prompt: Base rate 0.0035, sensitivity 0.89, false-positive rate 0.07. What is the positive predictive value, to three decimals?
base-rate.answer: The positive predictive value is about 0.043.

base-rate.title: A less rare condition
base-rate.prompt: Base rate 0.20, sensitivity 0.89, false-positive rate 0.07. What is the positive predictive value, to three decimals?
base-rate.answer: The positive predictive value is about 0.761.

base-rate.title: One percent prevalence
base-rate.prompt: Base rate 0.01, sensitivity 0.90, false-positive rate 0.05. What is the positive predictive value?
base-rate.answer: The positive predictive value is 0.009/0.0585, about 0.154.

bayesian-inference.title: Two unaffected sons
bayesian-inference.prompt: Prior probability 1/2 of being a carrier, likelihood 1/4 if a carrier and 1 if not, for two unaffected sons. What is the posterior probability of being a carrier?

bayesian-inference.title: A third unaffected son
bayesian-inference.prompt: Starting from posterior probability 1/5, a third son is unaffected, with conditional probability 1/2 if a carrier and 1 if not. What is the new posterior probability?

bayesian-model.title: Joint probability of a success
bayesian-model.prompt: Prior probability 1/2 on success probability 0.2, and one Bernoulli trial. What is the joint probability of that value and a success?

bayesian-model.title: Posterior after a failure
bayesian-model.prompt: Under the same two-point model, with prior 1/2 on 0.2 and on 0.8, the trial is a failure. What is the posterior probability of 0.2?

bayesian-probability.title: Ten-to-one odds
bayesian-probability.prompt: A bet of 1 unit in order to win 10 more units is taken on the favourable side. What probability does that commit you to, at minimum?

bayesian-probability.title: Three-to-one odds
bayesian-probability.prompt: A bet of 1 unit in order to win 3 more units is taken on the favourable side. What probability does that commit you to, at minimum?

case-control-study.title: Odds ratio
case-control-study.prompt: Cases are 24 exposed and 16 unexposed. Controls are 10 exposed and 30 unexposed. What is the exposure odds ratio?

case-control-study.title: Extra controls
case-control-study.prompt: Controls become 10 exposed and 34 unexposed, and the cases stay 24 and 16. What is the odds ratio?

causality.title: How many people differ
causality.prompt: Five people have treatment outcomes 1, 0, 1, 1, 0 and untreated outcomes 0, 0, 1, 0, 0. How many individual effects are nonzero?

causality.title: Corrected mean
causality.prompt: The third untreated outcome is changed from 1 to 0, and the treated mean stays 0.6. What is the average causal effect?
causality.answer: The untreated mean is 0, so the average causal effect is 0.6.

censoring-statistics.title: Product-limit value
censoring-statistics.prompt: Five units: one failure at time 2, a censoring at time 3, and two failures at time 5. What is the product-limit estimate at time 5?

censoring-statistics.title: Censoring becomes a failure
censoring-statistics.prompt: If the time-3 observation is a failure instead, what is the product-limit estimate at time 5?

classification.title: Bayes error with three classes
classification.prompt: Class probabilities are 7/10, 1/5 and 1/10. What is the conditional error of the Bayes classifier?

classification.title: A worse label
classification.prompt: At those same probabilities, what is the conditional error of announcing the class whose probability is 1/5?

classification.title: Two-class overlap
classification.prompt: Two class probabilities are 11/20 and 9/20. What is the Bayes error?

cluster-analysis.title: First single-link join
cluster-analysis.prompt: For the points A(0,0), B(1,0), C(5,0) and D(6,1), at what distance does single linkage make its first join?
cluster-analysis.answer: The first join is at distance 1, between A and B.

cluster-analysis.title: Within-cluster sum of squares
cluster-analysis.prompt: For the partition {A,B} and {C,D}, what is the within-cluster sum of squares?
cluster-analysis.answer: The within-cluster sum of squares is 3/2.

cluster-analysis.title: Distance between the pairs
cluster-analysis.prompt: Under single linkage, what is the distance between {A,B} and {C,D}?

cohort-study.title: Risk ratio
cohort-study.prompt: Of 80 exposed people, 20 develop the outcome. Of 120 unexposed people, 12 do. What is the risk ratio?
cohort-study.answer: The risks are 0.25 and 0.10, so the risk ratio is 2.5.

cohort-study.title: Extra exposed
cohort-study.prompt: The exposed group becomes 21 outcomes among 84 people, and the unexposed risk stays 0.10. What is the risk ratio?
cohort-study.answer: The exposed risk is 0.25, so the risk ratio is still 2.5.

conjoint-analysis.title: Best profile
conjoint-analysis.prompt: Brand A has part-worth 0, brand B has 2, the low price has 3, and the high price has 0. Which profile has utility 5?
conjoint-analysis.answer: Brand B at the low price, because 2 + 3 = 5.

conjoint-analysis.title: Brand share of range
conjoint-analysis.prompt: The brand range is 2 and the price range is 3. What share of the total range belongs to brand?

conjoint-analysis.title: Profile count
conjoint-analysis.prompt: Three attributes have 4 levels and two attributes have 3 levels. How many full-factorial profiles are there?

control-group.title: Small trial
control-group.prompt: A drug group has 2 deaths among 10 patients and the control group has 5 deaths among 10. What is the risk difference, drug minus control?

control-group.title: One more control
control-group.prompt: The control group becomes 6 deaths among 11, and the drug risk stays 0.2. What is the control risk?

correlation-does-not-imply-causation.title: Which risk is larger?
correlation-does-not-imply-causation.prompt: In the population of 20, treated mortality is 7/13 and untreated mortality is 3/7. Which is larger?
correlation-does-not-imply-causation.answer: The treated risk is larger, because 7/13 − 3/7 = 10/91 > 0.

correlation-does-not-imply-causation.title: Causal difference
correlation-does-not-imply-causation.prompt: If everyone treated gives 10 deaths out of 20 and everyone untreated gives 10 deaths out of 20, what is the causal risk difference?

correlation-does-not-imply-causation.title: Changed counterfactuals
correlation-does-not-imply-causation.prompt: If 8 of 20 would die if everyone were treated and 12 of 20 would die if everyone were untreated, what is the causal risk difference?

cross-sectional-data.title: Five incomes
cross-sectional-data.prompt: A snapshot of incomes is 2, 4, 4, 6, and 9. What is the mean, and what is the sample variance with divisor n-1?
cross-sectional-data.answer: The mean is 5. The sum of squared deviations is 28, so the sample variance is 28/4 = 7.

cross-sectional-data.title: Three units
cross-sectional-data.prompt: Values 3, 5, and 7 are measured once each. What are the mean and the range?
cross-sectional-data.answer: The mean is 5 and the range is 4. No within-unit change is defined.

data-collection.title: Sampling fraction
data-collection.prompt: A sample of 40 shops is drawn from 500. What is the sampling fraction?

data-collection.title: Larger sample
data-collection.prompt: The sample grows from 40 shops to 50, still out of 500. What is the sampling fraction?

data-quality.title: Bias of the mean
data-quality.prompt: Readings 22, 23, 21, and 22 are taken on a true length of 20. What is the bias of their mean?
data-quality.answer: The mean is 22, so the bias is 2.

data-quality.title: Fifth reading
data-quality.prompt: A fifth reading of 24 is added, and the true length stays 20. What is the bias of the new mean?
data-quality.answer: The mean is 22.4, so the bias is 2.4.

decision-problem.title: Radiotherapy score
decision-problem.prompt: With cancer probability 0.9, life expectancies 16.7 and 34.8 months, and a one-month penalty, what is the radiotherapy score?

decision-problem.title: No treatment
decision-problem.prompt: With the same probability, cancer expectancy 5.6 months and non-cancer expectancy 34.8 months, and no penalty, what is the no-treatment score?

decision-problem.title: Surgery at probability one half
decision-problem.prompt: Cancer probability 0.5, surgery survival probability 0.65, cancer expectancy 20.3, non-cancer expectancy 34.8, and a one-month penalty inside the survivor branch. What is the surgery score?
decision-problem.answer: The score is 17.2575 months, below radiotherapy at 24.75.

difference-in-differences.title: Two gaps
difference-in-differences.prompt: Treated means are 150 before and 140 after. Comparison means are 148 before and 146 after. What is the difference in differences of the post-treatment gap minus the pre-treatment gap?
difference-in-differences.answer: The post-treatment gap is -6 and the pre-treatment gap is 2, so the difference in differences is -8.

difference-in-differences.title: Changed comparison
difference-in-differences.prompt: The comparison group's later mean is 144 instead of 146. Treated means stay 140 and 150, and the earlier comparison mean stays 148. What is the difference in differences?

differential-privacy.title: Probability bound
differential-privacy.prompt: With δ = 0 and e^ε = 2, if the probability of S on database y is 0.1, what is the upper bound on the probability of S on a neighbouring database?

differential-privacy.title: A larger neighbour probability
differential-privacy.prompt: With δ = 0 and e^ε = 2, if the probability of S on database y is 0.3, what is the upper bound for a neighbour?

dimensionality-reduction.title: Sum of squares
dimensionality-reduction.prompt: The centred points are (-1,-1), (0,0) and (1,1). What is the total sum of squares?
dimensionality-reduction.answer: The total sum of squares is 4.

dimensionality-reduction.title: Horizontal fraction
dimensionality-reduction.prompt: If only the horizontal coordinate of those centred points is kept, what fraction of the sum of squares is retained?

dimensionality-reduction.title: Discarded sum of squares
dimensionality-reduction.prompt: What sum of squares is discarded by keeping only the horizontal coordinate?
dimensionality-reduction.answer: The discarded sum of squares is 2.

diversity-index.title: Concentration of 6, 3, and 1
diversity-index.prompt: Proportions 0.6, 0.3, and 0.1. What is Simpson's λ?

diversity-index.title: Unbiased pair estimator
diversity-index.prompt: Counts 6, 3, and 1. What is the unbiased estimator ℓ?

diversity-index.title: Equal split
diversity-index.prompt: Ten individuals split five and five. What is λ?

effect-size.title: Critical difference
effect-size.prompt: A standard error is 1.7 mmHg. What is 1.96 times that standard error?

effect-size.title: Shifted z-score
effect-size.prompt: The lower critical point is -3.332 and the true difference is -3, with standard error 1.7. What is the z-score?
effect-size.answer: The z-score is about -0.195, which rounds to -0.20.

effect-size.title: A larger effect
effect-size.prompt: The standard error is 2 mmHg and the true difference is -5. Using the critical value 1.96 times 2, what is the z-score of the lower critical point?

estimating-equations.title: Sample mean
estimating-equations.prompt: Observations 2, 4, and 6. What solves the sum of (y minus mu) equals 0?

estimating-equations.title: A second sample
estimating-equations.prompt: Observations 1, 3, and 8. What solves the same estimating equation?

estimating-equations.title: A second moment
estimating-equations.prompt: At mu = 4 for observations 1, 3, and 8, is the average of y squared minus (mu squared + 1) equal to zero?
estimating-equations.answer: No. The average is 74/3 minus 17, about 7.667.

expected-loss.title: Low base rate
expected-loss.prompt: Treat has losses 1 and 8, watch has losses 10 and 0, and the base rate is 0.2. What are the two expected losses?
expected-loss.answer: Treat has expected loss 6.6 and watch has expected loss 2.

expected-loss.title: High base rate
expected-loss.prompt: The same losses with base rate 0.7. What are the two expected losses?
expected-loss.answer: Treat has expected loss 3.1 and watch has expected loss 7.

expected-loss.title: Which action
expected-loss.prompt: At base rate 0.2, which action has the smaller expected loss?

experimental-error.title: Two treatments
experimental-error.prompt: Observations (3,5) and (8,10) have treatment means 4 and 9 and grand mean 6.5. What are the treatment and error sums of squares?
experimental-error.answer: The treatment sum of squares is 25 and the error sum of squares is 4.

experimental-error.title: Error mean square
experimental-error.prompt: The error sum of squares is 4 on 2 degrees of freedom. What is the error mean square?

experimental-error.title: A second split
experimental-error.prompt: Observations (1,3) and (5,7) have means 2 and 6 and grand mean 4. What are the two sums of squares?
experimental-error.answer: The treatment sum of squares is 16 and the error sum of squares is 4.

extrapolation.title: Negative aid
extrapolation.prompt: Using aid = 24319 - 0.0431 times income, what aid does an income of 1000000 produce?

extrapolation.title: Inside a larger income
extrapolation.prompt: Using the same line, what aid does an income of 200000 produce?

extrapolation.title: Four hundred thousand
extrapolation.prompt: Using the same line, what aid does an income of 400000 produce?

fat-tails.title: Two samples of five
fat-tails.prompt: Using divisor n, what are the moment kurtoses of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and of 1, 1, 1, 1, 6?
fat-tails.answer: The first kurtosis is 1.7 and the second is 3.25.

fat-tails.title: An exponential tail
fat-tails.prompt: For a unit exponential, what is the probability of exceeding 4, to six decimals, and what is the kurtosis of the law?
fat-tails.answer: The probability is 0.018316 and the kurtosis is 9.

fat-tails.title: Excess over the normal
fat-tails.prompt: A unit exponential has kurtosis 9. What is the excess over the normal value 3, and what is the survival past 1?
fat-tails.answer: The excess is 6. The survival past 1 is about 0.367879.

feature-selection.title: Intercept-only residual sum of squares
feature-selection.prompt: For the cases (x, z, y) = (0, 0, 1), (1, 0, 1) and (2, 1, 3), what is the residual sum of squares of the intercept-only fit?
feature-selection.answer: The residual sum of squares is 8/3.

feature-selection.title: Predictor x alone
feature-selection.prompt: On the same three cases, what is the residual sum of squares of the least-squares line that uses only x and an intercept?
feature-selection.answer: The residual sum of squares is 2/3.

feature-selection.title: How many best-subset models
feature-selection.prompt: Best-subset selection with 20 predictors fits how many models, and forward stepwise fits how many?
feature-selection.answer: Best subset fits 1048576 models. Forward stepwise fits 211.

federated-learning.title: Pooled mean
federated-learning.prompt: One site has values 1 and 3. Another has the single value 10. What is the pooled mean?

federated-learning.title: Unweighted gap
federated-learning.prompt: How much larger is the unweighted mean of the two site means than that pooled mean?

federated-learning.title: Equal sizes
federated-learning.prompt: If the second site instead has two values, both 10, what is the pooled mean?

first-international-statistical-congress.title: Opening date
first-international-statistical-congress.prompt: On what date did the congress open, and which commission called it?
first-international-statistical-congress.answer: It opened on 19 September 1853. The Central Statistical Commission of Belgium called it, with Quetelet presiding.

first-international-statistical-congress.title: Length of the series
first-international-statistical-congress.prompt: Nine congresses run from 1853 to 1876. How many years separate those two dates, and how long would each gap be if the eight intervals were equal?
first-international-statistical-congress.answer: The dates are 23 years apart. Equal gaps would be 23/8 = 2.875 years.

first-international-statistical-congress.title: Pooled rate
first-international-statistical-congress.prompt: Two compatible tables have 80 events among 200 people and 90 events among 300 people. What is the pooled rate?

game-of-chance.title: Euro die
game-of-chance.prompt: A fair die pays 1 on an even face, 2 on a 1 or a 3, and -3 on a 5. What is the expected payoff?

game-of-chance.title: Face value
game-of-chance.prompt: A fair die is scored by the face that appears. What is the expected score, and what is the probability that the face is at most 4?
game-of-chance.answer: The expected score is 21/6 = 3.5. The probability is 4/6 = 2/3.

game-of-chance.title: Wheel
game-of-chance.prompt: A wheel pays 4 with probability 1/4, 0 with probability 1/2, and -2 with probability 1/4. What is the expected payoff?
game-of-chance.answer: The expectation is 1/2, so the game is not fair.

harking.title: Expected false alarms
harking.prompt: Twenty independent tests of true nulls are each run at level 0.05. What is the expected number of results with p < 0.05?

harking.title: A stricter level
harking.prompt: The same twenty true nulls are tested at level 0.01. What is the expected number with p < 0.01?

harmonic-mean.title: Three interest rates
harmonic-mean.prompt: Rates of 5%, 10% and 15% produce the same income. What is the harmonic mean, as an exact fraction, and what is the arithmetic mean?
harmonic-mean.answer: The harmonic mean is 90/11 percent, about 8.182. The arithmetic mean is 10 percent.

harmonic-mean.title: Three weights
harmonic-mean.prompt: Person weights are 100, 200 and 300. What is the exact harmonic mean, and what integer does it round to?
harmonic-mean.answer: The exact value is 1800/11, about 163.636, which rounds to 164.

harmonic-mean.title: A zero
harmonic-mean.prompt: One of six positive observations is replaced by zero. What happens to the harmonic mean?
harmonic-mean.answer: The harmonic mean is undefined, because a reciprocal of zero is not a number.

hawthorne-effect.title: First-year peak
hawthorne-effect.prompt: A baseline of 100 units rises by 10 percent. What is the new level?

hawthorne-effect.title: Plant-wide gap
hawthorne-effect.prompt: On a baseline of 100, a 10 percent peak is 110 and a 1.4 percent rise is 101.4. What is the gap?

hawthorne-effect.title: Later peak
hawthorne-effect.prompt: A later peak is 20 percent above a baseline of 100, and the earlier peak was 110. How many units above 110 is the later peak?
hawthorne-effect.answer: The later peak is 120, which is 10 units above 110.

instrumental-variable.title: Wald ratio
instrumental-variable.prompt: The outcome means are 11 and 7, and the treated proportions are 0.75 and 0.25. What is the instrumental-variable estimand?

instrumental-variable.title: Weaker first stage
instrumental-variable.prompt: The treated proportion at Z = 1 falls from 0.75 to 0.65. The other values stay 11, 7, and 0.25. What is the estimand?

inverse-probability.title: One success
inverse-probability.prompt: One trial is a success and the unknown chance is uniform on the unit interval. What is the posterior probability that the chance exceeds 1/2?

inverse-probability.title: One failure
inverse-probability.prompt: One trial is a failure and the unknown chance is uniform on the unit interval. What is the posterior probability that the chance exceeds 1/2?

k-anonymity.title: Minimum frequency
k-anonymity.prompt: Three rows share one quasi-identifier pair and one row has a different pair. What is the minimum frequency?
k-anonymity.answer: The minimum frequency is 1, so the table is not 2-anonymous.

k-anonymity.title: After one added row
k-anonymity.prompt: A second row with the rare pair is added. What is the minimum frequency, and is the table 2-anonymous?
k-anonymity.answer: The minimum frequency is 2, so the table satisfies 2-anonymity.

kruskal-wallis-test.title: Rank statistic
kruskal-wallis-test.prompt: Three groups of size 3 have rank sums 10, 15, and 20. What is H?

kruskal-wallis-test.title: A larger ranking
kruskal-wallis-test.prompt: Three groups of size 4 have rank sums 12, 24, and 48. What is H?

kruskal-wallis-test.title: Oil data threshold
kruskal-wallis-test.prompt: H is 13.64 and the chi-squared 5% reference with 3 degrees of freedom is 7.81. Does the test reject?
kruskal-wallis-test.answer: Yes. 13.64 is greater than 7.81, so the test rejects.

kurtosis.title: A short flat sample
kurtosis.prompt: For 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, using the divisor n inside the central moments, what is the moment kurtosis?

kurtosis.title: One large observation
kurtosis.prompt: For 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, what is the moment kurtosis with divisor n, and how does it compare with 3?
kurtosis.answer: The moment kurtosis is 3.25, which is above the normal value 3.

kurtosis.title: Six numbers
kurtosis.prompt: For 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 6, what is the moment kurtosis with divisor n?

lady-tasting-tea.title: Number of divisions
lady-tasting-tea.prompt: Eight cups are divided into two labelled sets of four. How many divisions are there, and what is the null probability of the correct one?
lady-tasting-tea.answer: There are 70 divisions. The null probability of the correct one is 1/70.

lady-tasting-tea.title: Three correct
lady-tasting-tea.prompt: In the eight-cup design, how many sets get exactly three of one kind right, and what is the null probability of a score at least that good?
lady-tasting-tea.answer: There are 16 such sets. Including the one perfect set gives 17/70.

lady-tasting-tea.title: Six cups
lady-tasting-tea.prompt: Six cups, three of each kind, must be split by naming a set of three. What is the null probability of a perfect score?
lady-tasting-tea.answer: There are 20 divisions, so the probability is 1/20 = 0.05.

least-absolute-deviations.title: Three-point line
least-absolute-deviations.prompt: For the points (0,0), (1,0), and (2,3), what is the sum of absolute residuals of y=1.5x?

least-absolute-deviations.title: Horizontal comparison
least-absolute-deviations.prompt: For those same three points, what is the sum of absolute residuals of the line y=0?

least-absolute-deviations.title: A second triple
least-absolute-deviations.prompt: For (0,1), (1,1), and (2,5), which line has the smaller absolute-residual sum: y=1 or y=1+2x?
least-absolute-deviations.answer: y=1+2x, with sum 2, against sum 4 for y=1.

likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.title: Mammogram ratio
likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.prompt: Sensitivity 0.89 and false-positive rate 0.07. What is the positive likelihood ratio?

likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.title: Posterior probability
likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.prompt: Prior odds about 0.003512 times a likelihood ratio of about 12.714. What is the posterior probability?

likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.title: A simpler test
likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.prompt: Sensitivity 0.80, false-positive rate 0.10, base rate 0.20. What are the posterior odds and the posterior probability?
likelihood-ratios-in-diagnostic-testing.answer: The posterior odds are 2 and the posterior probability is 2/3.

machine-learning.title: Reducible plus irreducible
machine-learning.prompt: A fixed fit has f(X)=10, f-hat(X)=7 and error variance 9. What is the expected squared error?

machine-learning.title: Perfect fit
machine-learning.prompt: If that same fit recovers f(X)=10 exactly, and the error variance is still 9, what is the expected squared error?

machine-learning.title: Another fixed fit
machine-learning.prompt: Now f(X)=4, f-hat(X)=1 and the error variance is 4. What is the expected squared error?

mean-absolute-percentage-error.title: Three forecasts
mean-absolute-percentage-error.prompt: Observations 100, 200 and 50 are forecast as 110, 160 and 80. What is the mean absolute percentage error?
mean-absolute-percentage-error.answer: The mean absolute percentage error is 30.

mean-absolute-percentage-error.title: Two forecasts
mean-absolute-percentage-error.prompt: Observations 80 and 120 are forecast as 100 and 90. What is the mean absolute percentage error?
mean-absolute-percentage-error.answer: Each absolute percentage error is 25, so the mean is 25.

mean-absolute-percentage-error.title: A zero observation
mean-absolute-percentage-error.prompt: One observation in the scoring period is 0. What happens to the mean absolute percentage error?
mean-absolute-percentage-error.answer: It is undefined, because the percentage error divides by the observation.

measurable-function.title: Payoff expectation
measurable-function.prompt: Outcome 1 has probability 1/3 and payoff 2; the group {2, 3} has probability 2/3 and payoff 7. What is the expectation?

measurable-function.title: A higher payoff on outcome 1
measurable-function.prompt: Outcome 1 now pays 5, and the group {2, 3} still pays 7 with probability 2/3. What is the expectation?

measurement.title: Two operators
measurement.prompt: Operator A's times 10, 12, 11, and 11 have mean 11. The true duration is 12. What is A's bias?

measurement.title: One more time
measurement.prompt: A's times gain a fifth value of 16, and the true duration stays 12. What are the new mean and the new bias?
measurement.answer: The mean is 12 and the bias is 0.

morans-i.title: Line of four areas
morans-i.prompt: Areas in a line have values 1, 2, 4, and 5, and binary neighbour weights with six nonzero entries. What is Moran's I?

morans-i.title: Sum of the weights
morans-i.prompt: For four areas in a line and binary weights on each ordered neighbour pair, what is the sum of all weights?
morans-i.answer: The sum of the weights is 6.

morans-i.title: Alternating values
morans-i.prompt: The same four areas and weights now have values 1, 2, 2, and 1. What is Moran's I?

multilevel-model.title: Clinic variance
multilevel-model.prompt: A random intercept has variance 9 and the residual variance is 3. What are the marginal variance and the within-clinic correlation?
multilevel-model.answer: The marginal variance is 12 and the correlation is 9/12 = 0.75.

multilevel-model.title: Within-clinic difference
multilevel-model.prompt: With residual variance 3, what is the variance of the difference of two observations that share a random intercept?
multilevel-model.answer: The shared intercept cancels, so the variance is 3 + 3 = 6.

multilevel-model.title: Another intercept
multilevel-model.prompt: A random intercept has variance 4 and the residual variance is 12. What are the marginal variance, the within-group correlation, and the variance of a within-group difference?
multilevel-model.answer: The marginal variance is 16, the correlation is 0.25, and the difference has variance 24.

natural-experiment.title: Route means
natural-experiment.prompt: Long-route times are 30, 40, 50, and 40. Short-route times are 20, 25, 30, and 25. What is the contrast of means?
natural-experiment.answer: The means are 40 and 25, so the contrast is 15.

natural-experiment.title: Extra short trip
natural-experiment.prompt: One more short-route time of 20 is added, and the long-route mean stays 40. What is the new contrast?
natural-experiment.answer: The short-route mean is 24, so the contrast is 16.

nonlinear-regression.title: Exponential versus line
nonlinear-regression.prompt: For the points (0, 4), (1, 2) and (2, 1.2), which residual sum of squares is about 0.0188, the exponential fit or the straight line?
nonlinear-regression.answer: The exponential fit has residual sum of squares about 0.0188. The straight line has residual sum of squares 0.24.

nonlinear-regression.title: Exact exponential
nonlinear-regression.prompt: The curve y = β0 exp(−β1 x) passes through (0, 5) and (1, 1). What are β0 and the residual sum of squares?
nonlinear-regression.answer: β0 is 5 and the residual sum of squares is 0.

nonlinear-regression.title: A quadratic mean
nonlinear-regression.prompt: Is the mean β0 + β1 x + β2 x^2 fitted by nonlinear least squares?
nonlinear-regression.answer: No. That mean is linear in the coefficients, so the fit is polynomial least squares.

normalizing-constant.title: Two successes
normalizing-constant.prompt: The kernel on the unit interval is theta squared. What is its integral, and what normalizing constant turns it into a density?
normalizing-constant.answer: The integral is 1/3 and the normalizing constant is 3.

normalizing-constant.title: One success in two trials
normalizing-constant.prompt: The kernel on the unit interval is theta times (1 minus theta). What is its integral, and what normalizing constant turns it into a density?
normalizing-constant.answer: The integral is 1/6 and the normalizing constant is 6.

panel-data.title: Balanced changes
panel-data.prompt: Three units change by +2, 0, and +3. What is the mean change, and how does it compare with a rise in the cross-sectional mean from 10/3 to 5?
panel-data.answer: The mean change is 5/3, and the wave means differ by 5 - 10/3 = 5/3.

panel-data.title: A missing second wave
panel-data.prompt: Changes of +2 and 0 are observed, while the wave means that can be computed are 10/3 and 9/2. What are the mean of the observed changes and the difference of the wave means?
panel-data.answer: The mean of the observed changes is 1. The difference of the wave means is 7/6.

panel-data.title: Two complete units
panel-data.prompt: One unit moves from 1 to 4 and another stays at 6. What is the mean change?
panel-data.answer: The mean change is 1.5, and the wave means differ by the same 1.5.

pearson-distribution.title: A bag of one hundred
pearson-distribution.prompt: For n = 100, between which values of p, to four decimals, is every draw size a trigonometric integral?

pearson-distribution.title: A one-sided curve
pearson-distribution.prompt: A Type III curve has p = 3 and gamma = 2. What are mu2, the memoir skewness 1/sqrt(p+1), and mu4/mu2^2?
pearson-distribution.answer: mu2 is 1, the memoir skewness is 1/2, and mu4/mu2^2 is 9/2.

pearson-distribution.title: Another one-sided curve
pearson-distribution.prompt: A Type III curve has p = 8 and gamma = 1. What are the memoir skewness and mu4/mu2^2?
pearson-distribution.answer: The memoir skewness is 1/3 and mu4/mu2^2 is 11/3.

polynomial-least-squares.title: Four-point quadratic
polynomial-least-squares.prompt: For (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2) and (3, 5), what are the quadratic coefficients and the residual sum of squares?
polynomial-least-squares.answer: The coefficients are 1.2, −0.3 and 0.5. The residual sum of squares is 0.8.

polynomial-least-squares.title: Straight line on the same points
polynomial-least-squares.prompt: What is the residual sum of squares of the straight line fitted to those four points?
polynomial-least-squares.answer: The residual sum of squares is 1.8.

polynomial-least-squares.title: Three-point parabola
polynomial-least-squares.prompt: What is the residual sum of squares when y = β0 + β1 x + β2 x^2 is fitted to (0, 1), (1, 0) and (2, 1)?
polynomial-least-squares.answer: The residual sum of squares is 0.

posterior-probability.title: Equal unnormalised weights
posterior-probability.prompt: Prior probabilities are 1/4 and 3/4, and the sampling probabilities of the sample are 1/2 and 1/6. What is the posterior probability of the first explanation?

posterior-probability.title: Equal prior probabilities
posterior-probability.prompt: The sampling probabilities stay 1/2 and 1/6, and the prior probabilities are both 1/2. What is the posterior probability of the first explanation?

probability-interpretations.title: A short record
probability-interpretations.prompt: A record of 10 tosses contains 3 heads. What is the relative frequency of heads?

probability-interpretations.title: A longer record
probability-interpretations.prompt: A record of 100 tosses contains 60 heads. What is the relative frequency of heads, in lowest terms?

random-error.title: Rod readings
random-error.prompt: Readings 9.7, 10.2, 9.9 and 10.4 are taken against a 10 cm reference. What are the mean and the sum of squared deviations from the mean?
random-error.answer: The mean is 10.05 and the sum of squared deviations is 0.29.

random-error.title: Error of the mean
random-error.prompt: For those four readings, what is the error of the mean against the reference value 10?
random-error.answer: The error of the mean is 0.05 cm.

random-error.title: Centred series
random-error.prompt: Readings 8, 10 and 12 are taken against a reference of 10. What is the sum of squared deviations from the mean, and the error of the mean?
random-error.answer: The sum of squared deviations is 8 and the error of the mean is 0.

ranking.title: A tie at the top
ranking.prompt: Rank 8, 3, 8 and 1, giving rank 1 to the smallest and average ranks to ties. What are the ranks in that order, and what is their sum?
ranking.answer: The ranks are 3.5, 2, 3.5 and 1, and they sum to 10.

ranking.title: A tie in the middle
ranking.prompt: Rank 4, 1, 4 and 9 with average ranks for the tie. What are the ranks in that order?

raw-data.title: Five times
raw-data.prompt: Reaction times 8, 11, 9, 10, and 12 are reduced to their mean. What is that mean?

raw-data.title: Sixth time
raw-data.prompt: A sixth time of 16 is appended to 8, 11, 9, 10, and 12. What is the new mean?

resampling-statistics.title: Bootstrap variance
resampling-statistics.prompt: For the sample 1, 2, 3, what is the variance of the bootstrap distribution of the sample mean?

resampling-statistics.title: Jackknife bias
resampling-statistics.prompt: For the divide-by-n variance of 1, 2, 3, what is the jackknife bias estimate?
resampling-statistics.answer: The bias estimate is −1/3, and the corrected value is 1.

resampling-statistics.title: Two-point bootstrap
resampling-statistics.prompt: For the sample 4 and 9, what is the average of the four bootstrap means of size 2?

robust-statistics.title: Absolute deviations
robust-statistics.prompt: For 1, 2, 3, 4 and 20, what are the sums of absolute deviations from the mean 6 and from the median 3?
robust-statistics.answer: The sums are 28 at the mean and 21 at the median.

robust-statistics.title: Squared deviations
robust-statistics.prompt: For the same five numbers, what are the sums of squared deviations from 6 and from 3?
robust-statistics.answer: The sums are 250 at the mean and 295 at the median.

robust-statistics.title: One wild point
robust-statistics.prompt: For 5, 5, 5, 5 and 100, what are the mean and the sum of absolute deviations from the median?
robust-statistics.answer: The mean is 24 and the sum of absolute deviations from the median 5 is 95.

rounding.title: Proportional shares
rounding.prompt: The exact shares 14.25, 7.5, 4.5 and 3.75 are each rounded half-up to an integer. What is the sum of the rounded shares?
rounding.answer: The rounded shares are 14, 8, 5 and 4, and they sum to 31.

rounding.title: A printed margin
rounding.prompt: Two printed proportions are 0.851 and 0.150. By how much does their sum exceed 1?
rounding.answer: Their sum is 1.001, which exceeds 1 by 0.001.

rounding.title: Three numbers
rounding.prompt: Round 2.5, 2.5 and 3.2 half-up. What is the sum of the rounded values?
rounding.answer: The rounded values are 3, 3 and 3, and they sum to 9.

sampling.title: Equally likely subsets
sampling.prompt: A simple random sample of 2 units is drawn from 6. How many equally likely samples are there?

sampling.title: Larger population
sampling.prompt: The population has 10 units and the sample size is still 2. How many equally likely samples are there?

scientific-control.title: Two means
scientific-control.prompt: Drug changes sum to 54 over 6 patients and placebo changes sum to 18 over 6. What is the contrast of means?
scientific-control.answer: The means are 9 and 3, so the contrast is 6.

scientific-control.title: Extra placebo
scientific-control.prompt: The placebo changes sum to 22 over 7 patients and the drug mean stays 9. What is the placebo mean?

secondary-data.title: Recorded risk
secondary-data.prompt: A file of 240 admissions records 30 falls. What is the recorded risk?

secondary-data.title: Found admissions
secondary-data.prompt: Twelve further admissions are added, 3 of them with a fall. What is the new recorded risk as a count?
secondary-data.answer: The file has 33 falls among 252 admissions.

spearman-s-rank-correlation-coefficient.title: Mild disagreement
spearman-s-rank-correlation-coefficient.prompt: Rank differences are 0, 0, -1, and 1, so the squared differences sum to 2, and n = 4. What is the coefficient?

spearman-s-rank-correlation-coefficient.title: Complete reversal
spearman-s-rank-correlation-coefficient.prompt: The squared rank differences for a complete reversal of four ranks sum to 20. What is the coefficient?

statistical-dispersion.title: Five numbers
statistical-dispersion.prompt: For 2, 4, 4, 7 and 8, what are the sample variance with divisor n−1, the average absolute deviation from the mean, and the range?
statistical-dispersion.answer: The sample variance is 6, the average absolute deviation is 2, and the range is 6.

statistical-dispersion.title: Seven family sizes
statistical-dispersion.prompt: For 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3 and 6, what is the range, and what is the average absolute deviation from the mean as a fraction?
statistical-dispersion.answer: The range is 6. The average absolute deviation is 76/49.

statistical-model.title: Fitted value
statistical-model.prompt: The line is y = 2 + 3x. What is the fitted value at x = 4?

statistical-model.title: Residual
statistical-model.prompt: The point at x = 4 is observed as y = 16, and the line y = 2 + 3x fits 14 there. What is the residual?

statistical-survey.title: Sample proportion
statistical-survey.prompt: Of 50 drawn households, 35 have a working alarm, from a city of 1000. What is the sample proportion?

statistical-survey.title: Larger draw
statistical-survey.prompt: Of 80 households, 60 have a working alarm. What are the sample proportion and the sampling fraction out of 1000?
statistical-survey.answer: The sample proportion is 0.75 and the sampling fraction is 0.08.

statistician.title: Four districts
statistician.prompt: District birth counts are 120, 80, 200, and 100. What are the total, the mean, and the largest share?
statistician.answer: The total is 500, the mean is 125, and the largest share is 0.4.

statistician.title: Three districts
statistician.prompt: Three districts report 30, 45, and 75 births. What are the total, the mean, and the largest share?
statistician.answer: The total is 150, the mean is 50, and the largest share is 0.5.

statistician.title: Smallest share
statistician.prompt: For the counts 120, 80, 200, and 100, what is the smallest district's share of the 500 births?

supervised-learning.title: Neighbour of 3
supervised-learning.prompt: Training pairs are (0, 0), (1, 0) and (4, 1). What label does one-nearest neighbour return at feature 3?

supervised-learning.title: Neighbour of 2
supervised-learning.prompt: With the same training pairs, what label does one-nearest neighbour return at feature 2?

supervised-learning.title: Training error
supervised-learning.prompt: What is the training error of this one-nearest-neighbour rule on the three training points, when each point may be its own neighbour?

survey-methodology.title: Response rate
survey-methodology.prompt: Of 200 drawn graduates, 140 reply. What is the response rate?

survey-methodology.title: Reminders
survey-methodology.prompt: Twenty of the 60 non-respondents later reply, so 160 of 200 have replied. What is the response rate?

systematic-error.title: Balance offset
systematic-error.prompt: Readings 21.4, 21.7, 21.2 and 21.5 are taken on a 20 mg standard. What is the estimated systematic error?
systematic-error.answer: The mean is 21.45, so the estimated systematic error is 1.45 mg.

systematic-error.title: Scatter around the shift
systematic-error.prompt: For those four readings, what is the sum of squared deviations from the mean?
systematic-error.answer: The sum of squared deviations is 0.13.

systematic-error.title: Gauge
systematic-error.prompt: A 10 cm gauge is read as 12, 11 and 13. What is the estimated systematic error, and the mean after subtracting it?
systematic-error.answer: The estimated systematic error is 2 cm, and subtracting it leaves 10 cm.

systematic-sampling.title: Interval and last label
systematic-sampling.prompt: N = 40 houses and n = 8, with random start 3. What is the interval, and what is the last selected label?
systematic-sampling.answer: The interval is 5 and the last label is 38.

systematic-sampling.title: New start
systematic-sampling.prompt: The start is 1, with the same N = 40, n = 8, and interval 5. What is the last label?

tail.title: An SAT cutoff
tail.prompt: SAT scores follow a normal model with mean 1100 and standard deviation 200. What is the upper-tail probability at 1190?
tail.answer: The standardised value is 0.45 and the upper tail is 0.3264.

tail.title: A standard point
tail.prompt: The standard normal lower tail at z = 1 is 0.8413447. What is the upper tail?

tail.title: An exponential cutoff
tail.prompt: For a unit exponential, what is the upper-tail probability at 2, to six decimals?

true-value.title: Error of the mean
true-value.prompt: Estimates 48, 53, and 51 are made of a true mass of 50. What is the error of their mean?
true-value.answer: The mean is 152/3 and the error is 2/3.

true-value.title: Fourth estimate
true-value.prompt: A fourth estimate of 48 is added, and the true mass stays 50. What is the error of the new mean?
true-value.answer: The mean is 50 and the error is 0.

uncertainty.title: Mean absolute deviation
uncertainty.prompt: Timings 5, 7, 6, and 6 have mean 6. What is their mean absolute deviation?

uncertainty.title: Fifth timing
uncertainty.prompt: A fifth timing of 8 is added to 5, 7, 6, and 6. What is the new mean absolute deviation?
uncertainty.answer: The mean is 6.4 and the mean absolute deviation is 0.88.

unsupervised-learning.title: Horizontal fraction
unsupervised-learning.prompt: For the points (2,0), (-2,0), (0,1) and (0,-1), what fraction of the sum of squares is horizontal?

unsupervised-learning.title: Vertical fraction
unsupervised-learning.prompt: What fraction of the sum of squares is vertical?

unsupervised-learning.title: Leftover
unsupervised-learning.prompt: If only the horizontal coordinate is kept, what is the sum of squared reconstruction errors?
unsupervised-learning.answer: The leftover sum of squares is 2.
